Standard laboratory findings typically reflect systemic inflammation but are otherwise non-diagnostic; however elevated production of interleukin-1 beta (IL-1β) and tumor necrosis factor (TNFα) in peripheral blood leukocytes has been reported in more recent literature [20-22]. panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (a, b). a: Sagittal and transverse T2-weighted MRI of the left knee in a PAPA syndrome patient showing diffuse synovitis, joint effusion, and subcortical bone marrow edema, consistent with the sterile pyogenic inflammatory arthropathy characteristic of PAPA syndrome. b: Clinical photographs of the same PAPA syndrome patient showing pyoarthritis sequelae: chronic increased left knee volume and a trauma-triggered inflammatory flare of the right ankle, matching the trauma-induced sterile pyogenic arthritis phenotype of PAPA syndrome.
panels.attribution_text: Fernandes et al. Clinical and Genetic Findings of the First Report of PAPA Syndrome in Brazil.. Case reports in immunology 2021. doi:10.1155/2021/6660937. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: (a) Magnetic resonance imaging of the left knee. Sagittal plane (left); transverse plane (right), T2-weighted contrast. Presence of an extraarticular infiltrative process with involvement of the subcutaneous tissue and epidermis; inflammatory infiltration of adjacent muscle tissue, without evident collections; small foci of inflammatory edema affecting the subcortical bone marrow; extensive synovitis in the patellar recess and intraarticular involvement. In the transverse plane, there is an increase in the inflammatory process, with volumetric impingement of the popliteus neurovascular bundle. (b) Clinical characteristics of the pyoarthritis. Sequelae with increased left knee volume (left); the inflammatory process in the right ankle caused by trauma from the buckle on footwear (right).
in_text_mentions: Of note, a magnetic resonance imaging of the left knee (Figure 1(a)) showed significant inflammatory arthropathy, with joint effusion associated with diffuse synovitis; extension of the inflammatory process into the periarticular soft parts affecting the popliteus and quadriceps muscle; extrusion of the medial meniscus; and small foci of inflammatory edema affecting the subcortical bone marrow of the trochlear sulcus and the medial femoral condyle, which may have corresponded, according to the radiological report, to the focus of incipient osteomyelitis.

bsequently episodes of left knee arthritis triggered by low-impact local trauma and a new episode of arthritis, this one in the right ankle, due to trauma secondary to the use of inadequate footwear (Figure 1(b)). In these episodes, the response to treatment with prednisone 1 mg/kg over 3 weeks was satisfactory, followed by gradual withdrawal. However, no specific measure could be accessed to infer the impact of the nonpreventive treatment with anti-IL1, as suggested in the literature. panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). A: Clinical photograph of the patient's sacrococcygeal skin lesion in a case report of PAPA syndrome. The in-text description calls these pustule-like lesions; the visible lesion is an erythematous plaque with central crusting, but the caption/in-text do not specifically label it as an ulcer. B: Clinical photograph of an old lower-leg scar in the same PAPA syndrome patient. The caption identifies it as a skin lesion on the left leg, and the in-text describes an old scar; attribution to PAPA is by case context rather than a specific captioned disease manifestation. C: Clinical photograph of facial skin lesions in a PAPA syndrome case. The image shows acneiform papules/erythema, consistent with the acne component of PAPA, but the caption does not specify severe nodulocystic acne conglobata.

in_text_mentions: entation. Scattered pustule-like lesions were observed on the back, with the largest one located at the sacrococcygeal region, measuring approximately 4 × 3 cm2, without ulceration or tenderness. An old scar measuring approximately 10 × 9 cm2 was observed on the anterior tibia of the left lower leg (Figure 2). There were no oral ulcers. No superficial lymph node enlargement was palpable. The heart and lungs showed no obvious abnormalities. There was mild tenderness in the right lower abdomen and around the umbilicus and mild hepatosplenomegaly. No abnormalities were found on joint examination.
